subject: Private endpoint egress onboarding — IP matrix & proxy options
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: ACME Security <secops@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Private endpoint egress onboarding — IP matrix & proxy options

Hi team,

Thanks for starting the onboarding work for the private endpoint deployment. Attached is a first-pass egress matrix that maps our control plane and runtime outbound flows to recommended allowlist choices. High-level asks from our side so we can finalize the runbook and produce the audit bundle: 

- Please confirm whether Acme will accept:
  * Static/pinned IPs from Redwood (we can allocate per-customer reserved IPs) OR
  * Domain/SNI-based allowlist only (we can provide stable FQDNs and attempt SNI pinning)
- Are you comfortable with outbound connections terminating through your corporate proxy (mutual TLS to proxy) or do you require direct-to-internet egress from your NAT?
- Any TLS inspection / packet capture restrictions we should document (we can provide cert fingerprints and OCSP stapling info).
- Required retention for egress audit logs and where to push bundles (S3 bucket or SFTP).

Attachments: egress-ip-matrix.csv (columns: flow, port, protocol, purpose, recommended-allowlist) and runbook-egress-failover.pdf (ops steps for fallback routing).

If you prefer a quick call to walk the matrix we can do 30 minutes this week — propose Tue/Wed morning PT.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Platform Ops — Redwood Inference
-----
Attachment: egress-ip-matrix.csv (CSV, 12KB)
Attachment: runbook-egress-failover.pdf (PDF, 220KB)
From: ACME Security <secops@acmehealth.com>

Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 14:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress onboarding — IP matrix & proxy options

Dylan —

Thanks for the matrix. A few clarifying items from our side before we sign off: 

1) Ephemeral IPs: we cannot allow broad ephemeral ranges. Any rotating/ephemeral addresses need to be constrained to a published CIDR / rotation schedule and tied to a PoP.

2) Audit evidence: we need per-connection metadata (timestamp, source tenant id, destination FQDN, TLS fingerprint, bytes transferred) for the first 90 days and an aggregated summary for 1 year. We prefer S3 delivery with bucket-level IAM you will push to.

3) TLS inspection: we do not perform MITM TLS inspection on the control plane traffic. If Redwood requires inspection for telemetry, we need an alternate channel (agent → Redwood ingest over mTLS to a dedicated endpoint).

4) SNI / domain allowlist: acceptable if you guarantee stable hostnames and provide all SANs/fingerprints up front. If exact IPs are required later we will re-evaluate but prefer hostname-based allowlisting for scaling.

We also have a couple of questions about fallback behavior if your primary control-plane POP is unreachable: do you support queueing + exponential backoff, and will any fallback attempt connect to an alternate region (which would change jurisdiction)?

Happy to take a 30-minute call today at 16:00 PT if that helps.

— ACME SecOps (secops@acmehealth.com)
Security Operations — Acme Health
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: ACME Security <secops@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 08:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress onboarding — IP matrix & proxy options

Thanks — great feedback. Quick responses inline: 

- Ephemeral IPs: we can provide either: (A) per-customer reserved static IPs (recommended for regulated customers), or (B) a limited ephemeral pool with published CIDR blocks + rotation schedule (24–168 hour rotation windows). We will include rotation metadata in the audit bundle.

- Audit evidence: we can deliver per-connection metadata to an S3 bucket you own. Payload will include timestamp, tenant_id header, destination FQDN, TLS cert fingerprint (SHA256), and bytes in/out. We will hold detailed raw logs for 90 days and daily rollups for 12 months.

- TLS inspection: we do not require MITM on the control plane. For telemetry/metrics you can opt into a mTLS push to an endpoint you control — we will provide client certs if you want that separation.

- SNI/domain allowlist: Redwood guarantees stable hostnames for 12 months per release; we will provide SANs, A records, and cert fingerprints in the final runbook. If you later require fixed IPs we can do a short carve-out and add reserved IPs to your account.

- Fallback behavior: runtime requests use exponential backoff (max 5 retries) and will prefer regional POPs in the same jurisdiction. Cross-jurisdiction failover is off by default; we only do cross-region fallback if the customer explicitly opts in. For mission-critical control-plane messages we also offer a queued delivery window (up to 24 hours) and an alternate TLS-only proxy endpoint under customer control.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm preferred allowlist mode (static IPs vs hostname/SNI) and S3 bucket details for audit delivery.
2) We produce a finalized runbook with exact IPs, fingerprints, and rotation schedule for signoff.
3) Marissa will follow up on commercial options for reserved egress IPs if you choose static allocation.

If that works, Marissa — can you draft the commercial appendix and a timing proposal for reserved IP procurement? Laura — looping you for ops signoff on the runbook once we have the customer's choice.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Platform Ops — Redwood Inference
-----
Attachment: runbook-egress-failover.pdf (PDF, 220KB)

Thanks everyone — this is excellent. Confirming commercial & timeline notes from Redwood: 

- If Acme requests dedicated reserved IPs we can commit to per-quarter reservations. Pricing appendix will depend on number of static IPs and whether you want per-region isolation (I attached a draft pricing snippet to the HubSpot deal).
- Project timeline: once allowlist mode is confirmed we can produce final IPs/fingerprints within 3 business days, and schedule a 2-hour ops handover for cutover.
- Next steps for Acme: please send the S3 bucket ARN + IAM role that Redwood should assume for audit delivery, or confirm that you prefer SFTP drop.

Quick note on procurement: if you prefer reserved IPs we will require a short paperwork addendum (1–2 page) to the MSA documenting IP custody and rotation obligations — I can send a prepared addendum for legal review today.

Happy to schedule the 30-min call Dylan suggested — available Wed 09:00–11:00 PT.

Best,
Marissa Cole
